notes: SHIP v1.14.422 - WORKSTREAM 2: A MASTER IS STAGED, COUNTED AND SHOWN BEFORE IT BECOMES YOUR SITE. THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES. Until now a Master file became the site the moment it PARSED. That is how a Master carrying cables and no hosts became active silently, leaving Forge to report the emptiness days later in a cold aisle - the investigation that cost most of a session and ended with the honest answer being look at column D of SITE-HOSTS. Parse has been pure since v1.14.415, so a candidate already touched nothing; what was still missing was the operator DECISION. THE FLOW NOW (spec 4.1/4.2). The candidate parses into a STAGING object that no technician surface reads and no cache is stamped against. Its counts are shown - site, RACKS, HOSTS, CABLES - with any warnings, through the app existing confirm door rather than a new sheet. It becomes active only when the operator taps ACTIVATE SITE. Cancel discards it. THE HARD GUARANTEE from section 4.2 - your current site has not been changed - is tested as a guarantee rather than written as reassuring copy: after staging and discarding, the active Master identity and filename must be byte-identical to before. ZERO HOSTS WARNS, IT DOES NOT REJECT (owner ruling). A cabled, unprovisioned row is legitimate data - established at v1.14.413, and the reason the earlier 0/0 RACKED field report turned out to be honest rather than a bug. So the summary reports what it found, names SITE-HOSTS as the place to look, and lets the operator decide. Refusing here would make a legitimate import impossible. A Master with no readable racks is the one case that is never offered for activation. ACTIVATION RE-BINDS THE PROFILE. activateStaged() is the only path from staged to active, and it binds ACTIVE_SITE_PROFILE to the newly activated Master - otherwise the section 10 identity check would report a mismatch the moment an operator activated a file on purpose. THE IDENTITY SPLIT NOW REACHES THE ASSISTANT. siteProfile_getContextBlock emitted only buildLead, a deployment-level field, so the one surface that tells the assistant who it is talking to knew nothing about the site authority or the person actually holding the device. Both are now named, and named DISTINCTLY, because conflating them is how work gets credited to whoever is accountable rather than whoever did it. SPEC DRIFT REPORTED, NOT PAPERED OVER: the workstream 2 gate criterion names buildContext(), which does not exist in this build - the real function is siteProfile_getContextBlock(). An alias was deliberately NOT added, because two doors for one thing is the defect this programme exists to delete. TESTS: new spec 14-master-staging.spec.js, nine tests, all green. Also added to the event-log spec: section 4.3 proven - an event logged under Master A SURVIVES a swap to Master B, still names Master A, and the tamper-evident chain still verifies across the swap. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep, enforced by the commit hook. No RACK SCENE LOCK term touched. ?legacy=1 unaffected. NOT IN THIS SHIP, BY OWNER RULING: the boot gate that would send an invalid profile to SITE SETUP. It is the single riskiest change available - 37 ships deep in unverified debt, and a misfire locks an operator out of a working app in an aisle. It waits until after a physical device pass. DEVICE-VERIFY: import a Master. You should now see a summary - site, racks, hosts, cables - and an ACTIVATE SITE button, instead of the file silently becoming your site. Tap Cancel once and confirm your existing Master is still exactly what it was. Then import again and activate, and confirm the counts you saw were the counts you got.
